segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
twenty-two years.
And in the third year of hers, the Romans made Gaius Julius—
one of the three consuls—
king;
and he was named Caesar,
because when his mother died they cut her open
and took him out of her belly.
And he went down to Egypt
and confirmed the kingdom to Cleopatra.
And in that same year he became king,
the month Quintilis was called Julius.
And when Julius had reigned in Rome four years, he died.
And after him Augustus Caesar reigned fifty-seven years.
And in his sixth year,
Hyrcanus the high priest was taken captive to the country of the Parthians, that is, the Persians.
And for this reason Herod, the son of Antipater, the son of Herod the priest of the idol-temple of Apollo near the wall of Ashkelon, went up to Rome.
And from there he received the kingdom over the Jews,
and reigned thirty-seven years.
And when Hyrcanus returned from captivity,
Herod killed him and his son Jonathan in the eleventh year of Augustus.
And here the word of prophecy was fulfilled,
that 'the sceptre shall not depart from Judah until He comes whose kingdom it is.'
For in the time of this Herod the birth of our Saviour took place,
and the seven weeks and sixty-two weeks of Daniel were fulfilled,
which make four hundred and eighty-three years,
which begin from the sixth year of Darius the son of Hystaspes.
For that Herod, when he came from Rome and the Jews did not receive {OCR: accept} him,
fought and conquered,
and destroyed both walls of Jerusalem,
and destroyed many [people].
And he took the robe of the high priesthood under his own hand,
and would not leave a high priest [in office] except for one year.
And when he killed Hyrcanus,
he sent to Babylon and brought from there a man whose name was Ananel,
not of the family of the priests,
and made him high priest for one year,
and deposed him.
And he made Aristobulus, the son of Hyrcanus, who was the brother of Herod's own wife.
And after a little while he killed him,
and Mariamne his sister, who was his wife,
and their mother,
and altogether everyone who was of the lineage of the high priests.
And again he appointed Ananel.
And in the thirteenth year of Augustus, Antoninus {OCR: Antony}, the commander of his army, rebelled against him,
and loved {OCR: 88?}
